key_insight: The paper shows that vanilla on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) is just the special case β = 1 of a broader policy-optimization framework. By exposing β as a tunable KL-regularization weight, the method turns a brittle training recipe into a controllable one.
problem_solved: OPSD can improve reasoning language models, but in practice it is fragile and often requires heavy engineering to stabilize. This work addresses the lack of a clear, controllable formulation behind that instability.
method: Re-derive OPSD as a policy-optimization objective with an explicit KL penalty to a reference policy.
Generalize the objective with a β parameter that controls how strongly the student is anchored to the reference model.
Use this reinterpretation to make self-distillation training easier to tune and more reliable in practice.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a cleaner way to understand and stabilize self-distillation for reasoning models. It can reduce trial-and-error engineering by making the trade-off between exploration and trust in the reference policy explicit.
visual_elements: A side-by-side flow diagram comparing vanilla OPSD vs. β-OPSD
A simple slider graphic showing β controlling KL strength from weak to strong anchoring
A loss-function schematic highlighting policy reward and KL regularization terms
A stability plot illustrating brittle training at β = 1 versus improved robustness at other β values
paper_title: $β$-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation
paper_authors: Jiawei Xu, Minghui Liu, Juzheng Zhang, Tom Goldstein, Furong Huang
